reason: The story never says steam is hot or can burn; Grandma invites Maria next to the steaming pot and she steps back only one step with no reason given. The fact (steam can burn, so stay back) is not conveyed.
The story never says blocks, dolls and balls are toys; blocks and dolls only go into a toy box, and the ball is never grouped with them. The category fact is not stated.

"My eyes were open. That is why you could not find me!" The story ends on this without correcting it. Sam could not find Matteo because he hid behind the hill; having his own eyes open did not hide him.
The fact is about a grown-up checking bath water before you get in; the story is only about hose water in the backyard and never mentions a bath.

'It rolled to the wrong net! ... That one is the other team’s net!' In soccer you score by getting the ball into the other team's goal, so the other team's net is the right one; the story then contradicts itself by scoring in it.
The fact is that red, yellow and blue are called the primary colours; the story lists the three colours but never uses the words 'primary colours'.
'The book has to come back on its due day.' The term is 'due date', not 'due day'; the story teaches the wrong name for it.
'One rhymed with two in the song.' 'One' does not rhyme with 'two'; in the rhyme 'two' rhymes with 'shoe'.
The story never uses or defines the word 'season'; it says 'So the team was all of it', calling the practices and games 'the team' instead of the season.
'His hand came out the window and waved from where he sat,' shown as correct bus behavior. School bus rules say to keep hands and arms inside the window.
'The next day, something tiny and green was peeking out of the dirt.' Garden seeds take several days or more after watering to sprout and come up, not one night.
'They all sat dark and empty' and then Daddy lit them with a match. A diya burns oil through a wick; an empty clay lamp cannot be lit (the story also drops that diyas are oil lamps).

"Clara picked it up and put it back. Then she counted again. One, two, three, four." With the crayon put back she has five, and taking one away from five leaves four, not three; the counts in the story are wrong.
"You taste your food with those teeth, don't you?" (the dentist). We taste food with our tongue, not our teeth.
The story shows the ball going into the net but never says that this scores a goal for the team. It also never mentions the other team's net.
The story never conveys that darkness makes colors hard to tell; Luca finds things in the dark tent by touch and the story is about shape, not color.
'Mom sat in front with a little bundle... "I will hold him," said Mom.' A newborn must ride buckled in a rear-facing car seat, never held in a grown-up's arms in a moving car.
The story never conveys that toys cannot really feel; Mia's 'He is hurt. He is scared' is played along with and never framed as pretend.
'He counted to ten. Then he touched the butter. It was soft now.' Fridge butter takes tens of minutes at room temperature to soften, not ten seconds.
'"So Saturday comes after all seven days?" he asked. "Yes," said Mom.' The number of days until Saturday depends on what day it is today; it is not always seven.
'He rubbed his hands. One, two, three rubs. The mud went down.' Handwashing before eating needs soap and about 20 seconds of scrubbing, not three rubs with plain water.
The story never shows or says that a library puts books on shelves in groups. The "library" is toys lined up on a bench, and the book turns up in a box.
"The water cup tipped and the water did not spill, because the cup was round and it rolled back." Being round does not make a tipped cup roll back upright. A tipped cup usually spills or rolls away.
'The dots went up. Felix played louder. The dots went down. Felix played soft.' How high a note sits shows its pitch (or, for drums, which drum to hit), not how loud to play.
The card only shows where the party is. It is never called an invitation and never says when the party is.
'Mama knocked on the oven top. "All cool," she said.' An oven that has just finished baking is hot, not cool. Also fact_missing: the story shows two holes but never uses the word 'nostrils'.
'Grandma slid a soft toy bee across the table... Six bees, four buttons.' She gives one bee, not six, and the rows held ten buttons, not four, so this counting lesson models a wrong count.
The story says the bag goes into 'a machine' but never says the machine checks what is inside the bag.

'Iris tapped the top of the screen and the app closed.' Tapping the top of a tablet screen does not close an app; you swipe up or press the home button. Also fact_missing: the story says 'small pictures' but never uses the word 'icons'.
Dad says Eric 'made up the story' and 'made this book', but the word 'author' is never used and never defined as the person who wrote the words.
The story shows a drippy nose but never mentions a cold, so it does not say that a cold can make your nose runny or stuffy.
'The ends of the lines matched. Star, star, are, high.' In 'Twinkle, Twinkle' star rhymes with are and high rhymes with sky; high does not match star.
The fact says a day goes morning, afternoon, evening, night; the story only covers morning and afternoon and never mentions evening or night.
The story has Nana say "We say Bismillah first" but never gives its meaning, "in the name of God", and never ties it to Muslims.
"He started the R on the left this time. A, then Y, then A, then N." That spells RAYAN, not Ryan (R-Y-A-N), yet the librarian reads it as "Ryan."

The story never says that Arabic or Hebrew are read right to left; it treats the book that opens from the other side as if it was upside down ("The words were all at the wrong end!") and has him flip it.
'She made a big round B. Then two little r's.' The name Brielle has only one r (B-r-i-e-l-l-e, seven letters); Brielle's denial of seven letters is also left uncorrected.
The story never says babies wear diapers because they cannot use the toilet yet; the girl's 'Why so many diapers?' goes unanswered.
The story shows a heavy box and a light pillow but never says heavy and light are opposites.
Grandpa writes 'DOG' in capitals, then the story says its D 'faced the other way' from b. A capital D faces the same way as b; only lowercase d faces the other way.
'"Dry it?" he asked. "It will dry fast," said Grandma.' Max wrote with a pencil; pencil marks are not wet and do not need to dry.
The story shows dust getting in Anna's eye and asks 'Did they stop the dust?' but never says that eyelashes help keep dust and dirt out of the eyes.
'She dipped her brush in the red... But the red came out brown and muddy.' A brush with yellow on the tip dipped in red makes orange, not brown; red and yellow mix to orange.

'Ivy held up her little hand. Mom touched each finger. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven."' A hand has five fingers, not seven. Also 'Seven more sleeps until Saturday' wrongly treats days-in-a-week as days-until-Saturday after Mom said Saturday was not tomorrow.
Miss Jo helps Matteo, but the story never calls her a teacher or says a teacher is the grown-up who looks after and helps the children in a class.

'"Sophie, that net is not ours," she said.' The coach steers Sophie away from the net because it is not theirs, implying a team scores in its own net; a team scores in the other team's goal. Also, 'Sophie picked up the ball' is not allowed for soccer field players.

The story never conveys that the doll cannot really feel; Raphael's question 'Do dolls cry?' goes unanswered and the doll's 'cold toes' are treated as real, so only the pretend half of the fact comes through.

'The strawberry tasted plain, like nothing much... The sweet taste came back!' With the nose pinched you can still taste sweetness on the tongue; you lose the smell-based flavor, so food tastes weaker, not plain.
The word 'illustrator' never appears; Daddy only says Mr. Lee 'is the person who paints the pictures for books', so the term the fact defines is never taught.

'That night, snow peas from Jules's plant sat on his plate.' Snow peas are eaten pod and all while the peas inside are still flat; the round peas shelled from popped pods are garden (shelling) peas, not snow peas.
'Later, when the clock says two.' ... 'The big hand was at the two now.' At two o'clock the little (hour) hand points to 2 and the big hand to 12; big hand on 2 means ten minutes past the hour.

'The light was green, so they walked.' / 'they waited for green.' The story has them cross the road when the cars' light is green and the cars are moving; people should cross only when traffic has stopped and the walk signal is on.
'The M came before the A, not after.' In JAMES the M comes after the A, and the name has only one A, so the correction teaches a wrong spelling.
'Five is me, next year.' Ben is seven, and ages go up each year; next year he will be eight, not five.
'One bug,' he said. 'Ten legs.' Mom encourages counting a bug's legs to ten; insects have six legs (spiders have eight).
The story shows counting backward from ten to one but never says this is called a countdown.
"He drew two straight sticks for his H. One, two!" A capital H is made of three straight lines: two tall sticks and a line across.
'Now this book is yours to take home' / 'The card made the book hers!' A library card lets you borrow a book for a while; the book still belongs to the library and must be returned.
'painted the heart red with her pencil.' A regular writing pencil makes gray marks; it cannot color something red.

'Sarah held up her little hand. She counted her fingers. One... seven. Seven fingers.' One hand has five fingers; the story also implies it is always seven days until Saturday instead of stating a week has seven days.
'She slid the gloves back on, one by one, and they were smooth and clean.' A dentist does not take off gloves and put the same ones back on; used gloves are thrown away and fresh ones put on.
'Ten little duck toes,' said Arya (uncorrected, and she then corrects Dad). A duck has four toes on each foot, eight in all.
'He picked up the last block... "Here," he said. "Now we both have six."' Handing his seventh block to Mia would leave him six and her seven, not six each.

'Then she got to a letter that looked like a stick and a loop... "M," she read.' The letter M is made of straight lines and has no loop (a stick and a loop is P or b). Also 'A says ahh' is off: short A is the sound in apple.
'A wet spoon had sat on the paper. Where Jackson wrote, the letters turned dark blue!' Pencil marks do not turn blue on wet paper; pencil lead stays gray.
'The next morning, something green peeked up.' Carrot seeds take one to three weeks to sprout after watering, not one night.
'It smelled a little stinky, like all paints do.' Not all paints smell stinky; many children's paints have little or no smell.
The story shows tapping a small picture to open the app but never says the small pictures are called icons.
The story uses red, yellow and blue and mixes them correctly but never says they are called the primary colours.
'Is it tomorrow now?' 'Yes, it is tomorrow.' When the next day comes, it is called today; tomorrow is always the day after today.
'The sun was low, not high. So it was not morning.' The sun is low in the morning and evening and high around midday, so a low sun does not show it is afternoon rather than morning.
